2609.27593.title: Hidden not Deleted: How Networks Suppress Entangled Features
2609.27593.paper_summary: Concept erasure methods that operate via linear projection assume that features occupy separable subspaces. We show this assumption fails under dense superposition: when two features are forced into an antipodal pair sharing a single subspace, state-of-the-art linear erasure destroys both, not just the target. Networks trained with gradient descent instead solve this problem non-linearly, but not uniformly: they converge to one of two distinct circuit-level solutions depending on initialization, which we call mirror and shadow solutions. We map this bifurcation as a function of feature entanglement, show it reflects a stable attractor structure rather than an artifact of our setup, and use targeted causal interventions to demonstrate that both solutions leave a substantial, measurable trace of the erased feature's representation intact, recoverable through a single scalar patch rather than requiring any further training. This mirrors a failure mode recently observed empirically in LLM unlearning, where suppression rather than deletion allows forgotten knowledge to resurface; our results offer a mechanistic, causally-validated account of why that failure mode occurs.
2609.27593.paper_summary_zh: 概念抹除方法透過線性投影運作，假設特徵佔據可分離的子空間。<lb/>我們顯示這一假設在密集重疊下失效：當兩個特徵被迫進入共享單一子空間的對立對時，最先進的線性抹除會摧毀兩者，而不僅僅是目標特徵。<lb/>使用梯度下降訓練的網絡則以非線性方式解決這個問題，但並不均勻：它們根據初始化收斂到兩個不同的電路級解決方案之一，我們稱之為鏡像解和影子解。<lb/>我們將這一分岔映射為特徵纏結的函數，顯示它反映了一個穩定的吸引子結構，而不是我們設置的產物，並使用有針對性的因果干預來證明這兩個解決方案都留有被抹除特徵的表示的實質、可測量的痕跡，這些痕跡可以通過單一的標量補丁恢復，而不需要進一步的訓練。<lb/>這與最近在LLM學習遺忘中實證觀察到的失效模式相似，在這種情況下，抑制而非刪除使得被遺忘的知識重新浮現；我們的結果提供了一個機制性、因果驗證的解釋，說明為什麼會發生這種失效模式。
